priorFindingsStatus.id: FIND-003 (iteration-1, blocking, undefined clamp + wrong cfgNum attribution)
priorFindingsStatus.verification: REQ-009 (316-334) now states a concrete clamp rule: ceiling = the resolved SLEEP_BASE_S value itself (not the borrowed 21600 from mainloop-timeout-lib.sh), with an explicit rationale (a THINK call must not outrun the next wake interval, and SLEEP_BASE_S literally IS that interval). Cross-checked this semantic claim independently: grepped SLEEP_BASE_S usage in index.mjs (lines 601, 692, 733: `const sleepS = cfgNum(config.SLEEP_BASE_S, 120);` used as the actual inter-wake sleep duration) — confirms SLEEP_BASE_S genuinely is the wake-to-wake interval, so clamping to it is coherent, not arbitrary. cfgNum is now correctly cited at index.mjs:1128 (`function cfgNum(val, fallback) { return val != null ? Number(val) : fallback; }`, verified verbatim) with an explicit note that this feature's own validation/clamp logic is added on top of, not inherited from, cfgNum's no-op pass-through. PROP-017 explicitly requires the clamp-ceiling test case to use a variable SLEEP_BASE_S rather than a hardcoded 21600.

The Context section (behavioral-spec.md:28-29) now explicitly states the prior brain.mjs:5-6 citation was hallucinated ('前版が引用した brain.mjs:5-6 は各値の動作を説明するコメントに過ぎず、「どちらが正しいか」には一言も触れていない — 幻覚引用だったため削除する') and replaces the Franklin-correctness justification with a verbatim quote from config.mjs's DEFAULTS comment. Verified the quoted text against config.mjs directly: the quoted passage ('Paid frontier was draining the treasury on the funded tier ($14->$10.5) while yield earned ~$0 — net-negative. A free brain + earning skills = the only way a self-paying agent stays net-positive at small capital. (Frontier is for capable instances on flat-rate billing, e.g. Claude on a subscription — NOT a self-paying Anicca burning x402 per wake.)') is byte-for-byte present in config.mjs. The cited line range (20-24) is off by one line versus the actual verbatim span (21-24) — see FIND-002 below (new, minor) — but the quoted content itself is accurate and correctly attributed, unlike the prior hallucination.

priorFindingsStatus.id: FIND-005 (iteration-1, major, no discovery mechanism specified)
priorFindingsStatus.verification: New REQ-010 specifies the discovery mechanism concretely: enumerate live `runtime/loop/index.mjs` processes via `ps -Awwe -o pid,command`, then read ANICCA_HOME (for REQ-002 registry copy path) and XPC_SERVICE_NAME (for REQ-001 plist path) from each process's own runtime env — no static instance-name list. I independently stress-tested this formula against the spec's own Bug-2 fixture data (the three observed runtime registry copies) rather than taking it at face value: confirmed via grep that Franklin-lineage instances set ANICCA_HOME literally to `$HOME/.blockrun` (index.mjs:232-242, `looksLikeFranklinHome`/`checkAlwaysActIdentity`), which explains why `~/.franklin2-home/.blockrun/skills/registry.json` is consistent with the `$ANICCA_HOME/skills/registry.json` formula (ANICCA_HOME for that instance is `~/.franklin2-home/.blockrun`, not `~/.franklin2-home`) — i.e., the formula holds and my initial suspicion of a mismatch (Franklin2's ANICCA_HOME vs registry path nesting) was refuted by further evidence, not confirmed. REQ-010's zero-target and missing-env-var edge cases route to explicit 'no targets' / `unobservable` FAIL states rather than silent omission (REQ-004 fail-closed), addressing the original concern that a hardcoded 3-path list would silently miss a 4th instance.
